findings.mechanism: startHeartbeat registers a setInterval whose closure captures the Session. The timer is never cleared: Session.close() and Gateway.release() do not clearInterval(session.heartbeat), and beat() just returns when session.closed. The unref() only stops the timer keeping the process alive; it stays in Node's timer list and keeps firing every heartbeatMs. The closure keeps each closed Session reachable, along with its Decoder buffer, 64-entry recent message list, topic set and socket (LoopbackSocket.written frames).
findings.cause: heartbeat interval timer not cleared on session close (gateway.js:19 creates it, gateway.js:28 release and session.js:70 close never cancel it)
findings.evidence: Ran 4 waves of runWorkload(5000) in one process, with gc forced. Sessions and topics were 0 after each wave, but heapUsed after GC grew 24.1, 44.6, 65.0, 85.3 MB, about 20 MB per wave. With a scratch wrapper that calls clearInterval(session.heartbeat) in Gateway.release, heap stayed flat at 3.8, 4.0, 4.1, 4.0 MB. Source files were not modified.

findings.mechanism: Router.topics map of topic to Set of sessions
findings.cause: Session.close unsubscribes every topic and unsubscribe deletes empty topic entries
findings.discriminator: topics.size == 0 and sessions.size == 0 after each wave; the Gateway.sessions map is also emptied by release

findings.mechanism: Metrics counters map and latency array
findings.cause: keys come from a fixed set of names (closed_<reason> uses a few fixed reasons), and the latency array has fixed length
findings.evidence: code review; with the timer cleared, heap stays flat at about 4 MB across waves
findings.discriminator: key cardinality is bounded and does not depend on session count

findings.cause: capped at RECENT_LIMIT=64 with shift(), and per session only
findings.evidence: code review; flat heap once the timer is cleared
findings.discriminator: bounded per session, and freed with the session once the timer no longer references it
